title: Softlock when interacting with the pirate-hopeful protagonist

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, I’ve been playing through Game-1 on my Amiga and ran into a pretty annoying softlock related to the pirate-hopeful protagonist. When you interact with him after completing the “Gather the Compass” quest but before starting the “Set Sail” mission, the game freezes right after the dialogue ends. The music keeps playing, but the screen doesn’t update and none of the buttons do anything, so I have to reset the whole console.

I tried reloading an earlier save, but the same thing happens if I talk to him during this exact window. If I avoid him and just progress through the story until the “Set Sail” mission starts automatically, everything runs fine, but this is still a huge disruption for people exploring all the dialogue options. Has anyone else experienced this? Any workarounds until a patch comes through would be super helpful!

posts.cooked:
Hey, I ran into the same issue when I first tried interacting with the pirate-hopeful protagonist in the harbor scene. The game just freezes after you choose to accept his quest, and nothing else happens. It feels like the script doesn’t properly hand off control back to the player, which probably causes the softlock. If you save before talking to him, you’re basically stuck unless you reset without loading that save.

From what I gathered, it seems like the problem comes up only if you have a certain item in your inventory when you trigger the dialog. I tested by dropping everything except the essential quest items, and the interaction went through fine. It’s a weird combination, but at least there’s a temporary workaround until the dev team patches it.

Hopefully they release a fix soon because this side quest is pretty important to progress the story, and it’s a bummer getting stuck on something so early. In the meantime, make sure to back up your saves before talking to him, just to be safe!

posts.cooked:
Hey, I ran into the same issue with the pirate-hopeful protagonist in game-1 on my amiga. The softlock happens right after the dialogue choice where you agree to join their crew, right? I double-checked on a fresh save, and it consistently hangs on the loading screen right after that interaction. It seems like the game tries to trigger the next cutscene, but something fails to load properly.

From what I gathered digging around in the community, it might be linked to the event flags not setting correctly after that conversation, which traps the script in a loop. Some folks have suggested reloading an earlier save and avoiding that dialogue option, but obviously that’s not great if you want to experience the full story. Hopefully someone smarter than me can figure out a patch or workaround soon.

For now, if you want to keep making progress, try rushing ahead through other quests first and come back later to the pirate stuff once the devs have hopefully addressed the bug. I’m really hoping this gets fixed soon because the pirate-hopeful storyline looks super promising!

posts.cooked:
Oh man, I ran into the same issue while trying to get through that scene with the pirate-hopeful protagonist in game-1 on my Amiga. As soon as I try to interact with them, the screen just freezes and I can’t do anything — no joystick input or buttons seem to work, and I have to reset the whole console. It’s a total softlock, which is super frustrating since that character is part of the main story path.

From what I’ve seen, this bug seems to happen right after you pick up the crystal compass and then try to talk to them before heading to the docks. I think there might be some missing code or a flag that doesn’t get set properly, causing the game to hang indefinitely. Has anyone figured out a workaround? I managed to avoid the softlock by skipping the interaction and going straight to the market, but that means missing out on some dialog and side quests.

If any dev-types or code experts are lurking here, maybe there’s a way to patch the game or at least identify the exact trigger for this bug? I’d imagine it has something to do with event handling in that scene. Fingers crossed we get a fix that lets us enjoy that part without the risk of freezing!
